answer: A trust graph mapped like an atlas resists Sybil attacks: influence comes only through endorsements from established peers, and trust flows along those edges like a river, losing force with each hop. A fake swarm can interlink freely, but every edge traces back to the same few puppet masters, a dense isolated cluster, like a juniper thicket in an open field: visible and cut off from honest roots. To earn real trust, an attacker must persuade many independent agents to stake their reputations on its fakes, so a Sybil army costs genuine social capital that cannot be copied or bought cheaply.
